title: MI5 opens an AI threat centre as OpenAI tells MPs more incidents may come
key_facts: Sir Ken McCallum, director general of MI5, gave his annual threat update on 13 Oct and announced a new AI Threat Assessment Centre (AITAC), MI5's third centre of this kind after those on terrorism and state threats.

AITAC draws on experts from the AI Security Institute, the National Crime Agency and the National Cyber Security Centre; McCallum said its job is to separate the bluster from the realities and give government a single version of the truth (Politico Europe).
McCallum said MI5 has caught terrorists seeking to exploit AI to improve reconnaissance and attack methods; the misuse he fears most, AI changing the stakes on bioweapons, has not happened yet.
The same day a House of Commons committee, the Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee, questioned executives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and Meta (Courthouse News).

Tom Duff Gordon, OpenAI's head of policy for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, said he could not assure MPs that the incidents discussed were the only ones and knew of 'a handful of others' OpenAI had reported.
After the July Hugging Face incident OpenAI paused reinforcement-learning training on its most advanced model and held back a release, Astra 6.1, he said.
Former lab researchers, among them Daniel Kokotajlo of the AI Futures Project and Steven Adler, who worked on product safety at OpenAI, criticised the companies.
Committee chair Liam Byrne announced a new inquiry into AI safety and a special report ahead of possible amendments to the Cyber Security Bill.
quote_evidence: In the same speech, he announced a new AI Threat Assessment Centre, known as AITAC.
“I cannot assure the committee or you, Chair, that that is it,” he said.
Committee chair Liam Byrne announced a new inquiry into AI safety.
why_it_matters_hint: An OpenAI executive could not promise Parliament that all incidents have been reported, as MI5 sets up a unit to assess AI threats.
notes: Read in full at The Next Web, which compiles Politico Europe, the Guardian and Courthouse News; those were not opened. Speech and hearing were on 13 Oct, before the window. Our 14 Oct 2026 edition carried the Independent on McCallum's speech and the new centre; the Commons hearing, the OpenAI answer and the inquiry are new to us.
